projects.title: Hiking app
projects.description:
May 16, 2026

Built a mini travel app for our annual hiking weekends with Manu, Jonas and Fre. Lives at hike.kjellv.com. SiteGround for hosting. The brief was simple: one page per trip, photos, planning, costs, AI overview of the area, no database.

Stack ended up being PHP 8 with flat-file JSON storage. Stays out of the way on SiteGround's shared hosting, no Node process to keep alive, no migrations. All four user accounts live in `data/users.json` as bcrypt hashes. Trips and their meta (links, checklist, notes, comments, routes) are JSON files per trip slug. Deploys are `rsync` over SSH after a long detour fighting SiteGround SSH keys.

What got built: a Plannen tab (verblijf, links, checklist, notities), a Kosten tab with Splitwise-style settle-up math, an Over de regio tab where Claude generates a guide on trip creation (history, must sees, food, breweries, restaurants, transport, gotchas), a Foto's tab with upload + lightbox + +1 likes, and a Route tab with Leaflet on top of OpenTopoMap. The route tab supports multiple named routes per trip, GPX import, point-by-point editing, live geolocation, and even insert-between-segments when you click near an existing line.

Design pass landed on a Komoot/AllTrails outdoor aesthetic — Fraunces serif for display, Manrope for body, forest greens with terracotta accents, topographic contour pattern as background. Easter eggs in West-Flemish dialect surface as full-screen shoutouts ("wo zim?", "ist nog verre?", "we gon ton nog een drinkn zeker?", "'t'is oal betaald") at low probabilities on specific actions. Onboarding flow walks new logins through what's there and how to add the site to their iPhone home screen.

Most of the build happened in one long session with Claude Code. The friction was at the edges: SSH auth, image library quirks, browser cache invalidation. The core ships fast when you skip frameworks and database schemas.

projects.title: VC Rater
projects.description:
May 13, 2026

Day one. Spent the morning planning rather than coding.

Read the brand vault and the existing Spain Explorer codebase (same stack pattern). The product shape crystallised after some back-and-forth: internal tool first with a public-later horizon, where everyone shares the investor database but each user owns their scoring weights.

Picked Railway over Vercel + Supabase. Vercel's 60s serverless cap was a blocker for long Claude enrichment runs; Railway just runs everything as one long-lived Node process. One platform, one deploy, one Postgres.

Phase 1 deliverables: a controlled vocabulary (sectors, geos, stages, instruments, partner backgrounds, tier bands) and a hand-curated seed CSV of 79 EU robotics / hardware seed-to-Series-A funds, each with confidence flags. The vocabulary became the closed enum the scraper has to map free text into.

Phase 2 scaffold: Express + Drizzle + Postgres + Vite + Tailwind + Auth.js with a dev-credentials provider (no OAuth setup needed for local). Got the first sign-in working end-to-end. Hit a Vite-proxy bug where Auth.js trusted the upstream Host header (localhost:3010) and tried to redirect the browser there instead of 5180. Two-line fix to `changeOrigin: false`. Saved a memory rule about avoiding common default ports (3000 / 5173 / 5432) so future scaffolds don't collide.

Ended the day with 79 funds visible in the browser, signed in via dev login. Foundation in place.

---

May 19, 2026

Massive day. Built the matcher, expanded the catalogue, shipped the enrichment pipeline, and split admin from founder views.

Phase 4 first: a scoring engine with eight criteria, each with editable per-value preference matrices (per-sector, per-geo, per-tier, per-partner-background). Per-stage matrix replaced binary stage matching once I realised "Series A founders also pitch seed funds sometimes" is the real story. Refactored criteria from per-user to per-profile after pointing out the public-launch path needs each founder owning their own scoring playbook. Added PDF deck upload — pdf-parse extracts text, Claude returns structured signals, founder reviews and applies.

The list went from 79 funds to 204:
• 13 EU robotics specialists from Vestbee
• 25 robotics-dedicated US / Canada funds (DCVC, Lemnos, Playground, Eclipse, Material Impact)
• Country sweeps: Germany 43, UK 29, Netherlands 18, Italy 7, Spain 6, Nordics + Iceland + Luxembourg + Estonia filled out
• Added an `impact` sector tag so climate-leaning funds (World Fund, Planet A, Extantia) still match founders who care
• Lesson: aggregator-driven crawls systematically under-represent local-language funds. Miles Ahead only showed up because I flagged it manually

Then Phase 3 enrichment: cheerio for HTML, Claude Sonnet for structured output. For each fund it fetches up to five candidate pages, strips tags, sends the combined text to Claude with a prompt that returns stages / sectors / geos / instruments / cheque sizes / partners / tier / fund vintage. Ran the batch across 191 funds — 164 succeeded, 40 errored (JS-rendered SPAs cheerio can't see). Backfilled tier from training-data knowledge for the rest via SQL.

UX split: founders see only Matches (no Profile / Investors in nav). Admin (just my account) gets the Investors page as a deep dashboard with edit modal and inline status flags. 🚩 update-request flow, ⚠️ incomplete badge, pagination, null-as-zero scoring so missing data actually penalises.

Roughly $5–10 on the Claude API. Worth it.

projects.title: Hexking
projects.description:
May 4, 2026

Started with a half-formed board game idea: round or hexagonal, two teams of eight, surround the enemy king. By the end of the session it was deployed and playable in a browser.

The interesting part wasn't writing code. It was getting the rules right before any code existed. Claude asked the questions, I answered: turn structure, board size, movement, win condition, what happens when a king has no legal move. Fifteen-plus design questions before any scaffolding. The rules came out clean: 1-hex king, 2-hex soldiers, edges and own pieces count toward surround, lose if encircled for one full cycle.

A few things stood out:
• Constraints surface fast when you're forced to articulate them. "King moves the same speed as soldiers" sounds fine until you realize the king runs forever and no one can win. We flipped it: king moves 1, soldiers move 2.
• Writing the rules in plain English before any types or functions kept the implementation cheap. The entire game logic fits in one file.
• Minimax with alpha-beta at depth 2 is enough to feel like a real opponent in a small game. The AI doesn't need to be smart, just consistent.
• The "classical chess club" aesthetic took maybe twenty minutes once the game worked. Cinzel for headings, parchment hex cells, gradient stones with a gold rim on the king. Visual identity is mostly a typography choice.

Live in production by the end of the session. Vercel deploy handled by Kjell.

Then kept iterating. Three threads.

The "luxurious border" was the messiest. Chunky wood frame around the hexes: too much, looked stuck on. Smooth pointy-top hex outline around the playing area: too detached from the actual zigzag shape. The right answer was tracing gold along the literal perimeter edges, with each edge's drop shadow pushed outward along its own normal so the depth always lands on the dark side, never on the parchment.

For the AI: minimax depth 2 to 3 with root-level move ordering, plus a one-line bug fix that probably did more for difficulty than the depth bump. The eval was counting only pieces as "filled neighbors" of a king. Blocked hexes from maps weren't counted. So Sovereign was undervaluing every position where its opponent's king was pressed against a wall.

For replay value: four hand-designed maps (Open, Pillars, Wall, Quartet) with blocked hexes placed symmetrically across the y-axis. Blocked counts as wall toward surround, so you can use them as offensive geometry, not just obstacles.
learnings: Minimax with alpha-beta at depth 2 is enough to feel like a real opponent in a small game. The AI doesn't need to be smart, just consistent.

projects.title: Very Klear website
projects.description:
April 22, 2026

Started the retroactive interview process. Did leaf 2 (positioning audit) and leaf 3 (customer journey). The positioning one was the first to show what this process actually does — I told Claude that not every "that's interesting" in a demo is a positioning problem, often it's narrative ownership or a sales execution issue. Claude reshaped a whole section around that. The customer journey post got a similar treatment on the awareness gap: the underdog framing of "like Google Analytics but GDPR-friendly" works for small businesses but not for challengers, because it permanently positions you behind someone else.

This is the piece I keep underestimating — the articles sound fine when they're general, but the moment you put a specific opinion or a specific client pattern in, the whole thing gets sharper. And you can only do that with interview + edit, not by writing the first draft with perspective already in it. The perspective comes out in response to a question.

---

April 23, 2026

Long day.

Morning: retroactive blog interviews. The posts were already published, clean on framework, but too abstract — no client stories, no ZYGO, no Willow data, no actual Kjell. So for each post, Claude reads it, asks 3-4 targeted questions at the abstract spots, I answer, Claude edits. Got through leaf 9 (founder-led sales), 10 (content engine), 11 (LinkedIn), and 13 (messaging guide). The messaging guide one was the most interesting — I told Claude to look underneath the GTM dashboard for more substance, and it actually did. Pulled out the value trifecta, the onlyness statement, the adoption-group tagging on value props, the category/brand/use objection taxonomy, the motivators section. The article went from six thin sections to a real framework that mirrors how I actually do the work. The tool isn't the point, the discipline is. That line made it into the post.

Deleted four posts along the way: the three-page website one (didn't agree with the framing), the email sequence one, the three-failed-content-strategies post, and the GTM engagement description. Cleaned up all the cross-links. Messaging guide had gone orphan — no inbound or outbound links — so I reconnected it to ICP and positioning.

Halfway through I realised Claude was doing all the interviews off my in-the-moment answers, not reading my weekly B2B notes where half the concrete examples already live. Saved that as a feedback memory and baked it into four skills (write-blog-post, blog-briefing, blog-research, blog-interview) so any future blog work pulls from the notes first.

Afternoon: prep for deploy. Ran the build. Two pre-existing issues surfaced: `@tailwindcss/typography` was imported in the config but never in package.json (who ships like that), and one meta_description was 171 chars against the 160 schema limit. Both fixed. Added a privacy page at `/privacy` with the Belgian GDPR essentials — rights, third parties (Google Fonts, TidyCal), no cookies currently. Later added the legal entity details after I thought to mention them: Very Klear, Ligywijk 123, 8900 Belgium, VAT BE1014759659. Saved those to memory too.

Sitemap plugin kept crashing at build with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'reduce')`. Turns out the latest `@astrojs/sitemap` (3.7.x) uses the `astro:routes:resolved` hook which only exists in Astro 5+. We're on 4.16, so `_routes` stayed undefined. Real fix is Astro 6 (which also clears the audit findings — 9 CVEs, all in middleware/SSR/dev-server which we don't use), but Astro 6 means replacing `@astrojs/tailwind` with the Tailwind 4 Vite plugin, which is a Tailwind migration I didn't want to do tonight. Downgraded sitemap to 3.4.1, which works on Astro 4. Added `robots.txt`, a 404 page, favicon.

Evening: logo and fonts. Dropped three PNG wordmarks into `public/`: square stacked (for OG + favicon), horizontal transparent (for nav), horizontal cream (unused, ended up deleting). I use Fields as the display font in the actual wordmark. Shared the file — Fields Medium in OTF — and then Claude read the EULA. Desktop license. Explicit prohibition on CSS `@font-face` embedding. So the font file had to be pulled out of `public/` (anything in there ships publicly) and parked in a non-served folder. Fell back to Fraunces from Google Fonts, with the SOFT axis pinned at 100 to get the warmth close to Fields. Not identical but respectably close until I buy the webfont license.

Then the CSS completely broke. Tailwind integration wasn't auto-injecting. Classes were in the HTML but no stylesheet was being loaded. Traced it to `@astrojs/tailwind@5.1.5` + Astro 4.16 silently failing to run the `injectScript("page-ssr", ...)` hook. Fixed by disabling `applyBaseStyles` on the integration and explicitly importing a `global.css` from `BaseLayout.astro` with the three `@tailwind` directives. CSS back.

Late evening: homepage overhaul. Gave feedback on the homepage — eight changes in one message. Killed the Before/After section (duplicated the problem section above it). Fixed the engagement timeline where the horizontal line was crossing the phase badges (z-index fix). Killed the Deliverables section. Killed the Results section with the four stats — "they're tiny signals, you'd need 10+ for them to matter." Killed the ZYGO case study card (too soon to publish that). Replaced the reference-request CTA in testimonials with a Brent Schepers quote. Combined the two near-footer CTAs into one coral block. Blog cards made equal height.

Then a few structural additions. A "Who it's for" section with fit / not-fit / trigger-moments blocks, pulled straight from the GTM dashboard's ICP JSON. A "What's different" section with three archetypes (strategy consultant / freelance operator / Very Klear) + a dark card describing the GTM dashboard as the system behind the work. Language pulled straight from the dashboard's `market.json` and `messaging.json` — not invented. A "Recent writing" 2-card section auto-pulling the latest posts. Removed weeks from the engagement phases. Renamed the phases Diagnosis → Diagnose, Foundation → Build, Traction → Grow to match the blog categories (which was inconsistent). Updated the clients grid: removed Airwallex, Soldo, Ecommpay, Malt, Accountable, Mercury; kept ZYGO, ONAH; renamed Aspire to Aspire App; added Willow and SOFICO. About paragraph rewritten to reflect the actual range — fintech scale-ups, deeptech/robotics, HRtech, enterprise finserv, crowdfunding, taxtech, cybersecurity, venture firms. Seven categories. Not just SaaS.

The ICP shift. B2B SaaS is narrowing as a category. AI is blurring the line with services-as-software. The companies I actually work with span way further than traditional SaaS — ZYGO deeptech, ONAH HRtech, SOFICO enterprise finserv, Winwinner crowdfunding, The Harbour fundraising, cybersecurity, various fintechs. So across the whole site: B2B SaaS → B2B tech. Homepage, privacy, footer, meta tags, RSS, blog index, category pages, six blog posts, GTM dashboard JSONs. The one slug I didn't change was `linkedin-for-b2b-saas-founders` — changing a URL means a redirect — so the page title updated but the URL didn't.

Deploy. Zipped `dist/` (157KB) for SiteGround. First upload got a 403 because the dist folder contents went into a subfolder instead of straight into `public_html/`. Fixed. Kept `.well-known/` (Let's Encrypt validation). Deleted the "Awesome Site in The Making" placeholder.

Speed check. First visit cold: 3-6 seconds. Measured it with curl — 3.4s TTFB cold, 0.4s warm. DNS pre-resolved reduced it to 0.88s but SSL handshake alone was 0.5s. SiteGround shared plan, slow DNS and TLS. Biggest single fix is enabling Cloudflare on SiteGround — free, cuts cold connect by most of that. On the frontend side: shrunk favicon from 37KB to 6.8KB, narrowed the Fraunces variable-font axis range, added preload hints for the nav logo, added `fetchpriority="high"` on it. Removed a few unused assets. Then rebuilt and re-zipped.

Also saved a few feedback memories: read weekly B2B notes before any blog work (baked into four skills), suggest updating the Vibing note near end of session (this file), ICP is B2B tech not B2B SaaS, the Very Klear legal entity details.

---

April 24, 2026

Started the actual blog pipeline at 12:30am. Leaf 4: "the 'do everything' trap — why multi-channel marketing kills early-stage B2B tech startups." Writing a post about focus at past midnight is, as I pointed out halfway through, the exact problem the post is about. Pretty meta. Kept going anyway.

Ran the full `/write-blog-post` orchestrator: brief → research → write → review → interview. The brief and research came out strong — Claude pulled the ONAH/Sophie story, the Sales Nav confession from my Apr 14 note, Peter Thiel on single-channel distribution, April Dunford on positioning-as-input, and a consensus data point that ~80% of pre-seed traction comes from one channel (MKT1, Stripe, Boundless). The writer produced a 1,650-word draft in one shot. Reviewer flagged five minor fixes — primary keyword gap in title and H1, missing the 80% stat in the body, meta description 2 chars over, inline attribution on three data claims, small line edits.

Did the edits inline. Launched the interview agent. It asked five sharp questions back — whether to keep the Sophie session clean or tell the messier version, what the real emotion was underneath buying Sales Nav, what specific line recurs in five-channel-founder conversations, which of the four channel-filter questions does the heaviest lifting, and what the common pushback is. Answered four of five. The real emotion on Sales Nav wasn't tool-as-therapy, it was wanting a legitimate tool without the grey-area feeling of the scraper-of-the-month LinkedIn automation scene. That distinction is sharper than the generic framing. The pattern in five-channel-founder calls is the paradox: "I don't have time" + time spent on five channels that don't move the product. I've been there as a freelancer — going wide when business isn't going right, which always makes it worse. And the decisive filter question is always the same: where is your ICP? Everything else is downstream.

Got distracted revising the draft manually while the interview agent was mid-revise — ended up going faster than the agent because I already knew what I wanted to say. The meta-point stands though: this is how the pipeline is supposed to work. You get a draft that's 90% there, a reviewer that catches the craft issues, and an interviewer that pulls out the last 10% that only you can provide.
learnings: *Afternoon: prep for deploy.** Ran the build. Two pre-existing issues surfaced: `@tailwindcss/typography` was imported in the config but never in package.json (who ships like that), and one meta_description was 171 chars against the 160 schema limit. Both fixed. Added a privacy page at `/privacy` with the Belgian GDPR essentials — rights, third parties (Google Fonts, TidyCal), no cookies currently. Later added the legal entity details after I thought to mention them: Very Klear, Ligywijk 123, 8900 Belgium, VAT BE1014759659. Saved those to memory too.

*Late evening: homepage overhaul.** Gave feedback on the homepage — eight changes in one message. Killed the Before/After section (duplicated the problem section above it). Fixed the engagement timeline where the horizontal line was crossing the phase badges (z-index fix). Killed the Deliverables section. Killed the Results section with the four stats — "they're tiny signals, you'd need 10+ for them to matter." Killed the ZYGO case study card (too soon to publish that). Replaced the reference-request CTA in testimonials with a Brent Schepers quote. Combined the two near-footer CTAs into one coral block. Blog cards made equal height.

For the team interviews, I could build my own recording tool that will solve a couple of things for me. So if the recording tool can manage multiple projects and I can create a project, give it the questions of my project and then do the recordings with different members and it could automatically pass the replies from the recording, from the transcript to meet the right questions. And then if I put the different interviews next to each other, which have similar questions, then I could make compilations of all the questions for the same answer. So it's a bit like a mix between a recording tool and a form maker. If I do it with ZYGO branding, I think it would be really cool.

But maybe cooler if i don't use the typical flask approach, but make it publicly available with login and onboarding. Upon starting, you give a website and it takes the web branding to define the UI colours.

Plan looked great, but required to many external tools like supabase, whispr flow etc. so i'll start with a local MVP based on the usual stack.

Works nicely after a little debugging because the audio wasn't being parsed correctly. Hooking this up to my PA took surprisingly little time.

projects.title: Investment tracker
projects.description:
March 2, 2026

For over 10 years, i've been tracking my investments in a Numbers file. Over time, i've wanted to add more calculations and "features" but the more I add, the more I start to doubt the accuracy. So it was about time to code something.

The plan was defined rather quickly based on an csv of my existing file. 

---

March 3, 2026

Somehow the hardest app of all - just cant handle the existing data. two hours of debugging have only made things worse. Should I put the money I've spent on Claude down as an investment? It feels more like a waste at the moment...

Back to scratch is the only way i can see this working out. Trying a "soft" reset didn't lreally do it. Telling Claude to clean the existing databases didn't really work because he ran into another conflict half an hour later. 

So I told Claude to make an assessment and really start over. Judging from his reply, he agrees: "will be much faster than continuing to debug mysterious database issues".

---

March 4, 2026

Sometimes you really need to treat Claude like an intern. I've been rebuilding the app and database (I mean, Claude has been rebuilding it). But he used the same corrupted data. The whole idea behind the rebuild was to use the proper data and remove any duplicates or sources that could lead to confusion. 

After pointing this out, it seems to work. Now I'll just focus on getting everything right for me. .

Only thing left today, is adding some more graphs.

I'll also add more detailed data about yields: where they come from (interest, shares, other) and about individual investments.

---

April 1, 2026

Fixing the kids dashboards today. Taking it step by step. Just been describing what information I have, how it's currently organised and then letting Claude do its work. Voice isn't working in Claude Code, so I'm just talking to Mistral and then copy-pasting. At least that makes the subscription worth a few cents lol. 

I like that Claude intuitevely added a field for the money source and putt grandma as the example.

next month, need to continue with more details and sspecific tracking for shares

---

April 10, 2026

I spent a lot of time trying to get my data right, only to realise that the PostgreSQL is saved locally and can't be accessed on my other device.

So now I'm running the following migration and I'm scared to death that it will have errors and ruin my data:
Backup via pg_dump + JSON export
Swap schema from PostgreSQL → SQLite types
Swap driver from postgres → better-sqlite3
Push schema to create the SQLite file
Import data from JSON backup 
---

May 2, 2026

Tried to run my investment tracker this morning. Got `Cannot find module 'yargs-parser'` — a transitive dependency `concurrently` needed somewhere two layers deep. Hadn't touched the code. Couldn't be a bug. Reinstall would normally fix this kind of thing in 30 seconds, but every reinstall was happening with iCloud running underneath, which turned out to be the actual problem.

## The Diagnosis

iCloud Drive was evicting files inside `nodemodules` to save local disk space, replacing actual JavaScript files with placeholder stubs. When Node tried to `require('yargs-parser')`, it found nothing and threw. iCloud is built around the assumption that you have a few documents, not 50,000 tiny ones — `nodemodules` is basically its worst-case input.

The real diagnosis went one level deeper than that. I had two tools fighting over the same job. iCloud was syncing the whole project (because the project lived inside iCloud Drive). And Git — once I added it during the cleanup — was tracking the SQLite database file. Both wrong. Code shouldn't sync via iCloud; data shouldn't sync via Git.

## The Fix

Split the responsibilities cleanly: code through Git, data through iCloud, glued together with a symlink.
• Code lives outside iCloud now, in `~/Projects/`. Synced across devices through a private GitHub repo.
• The SQLite database stays in iCloud at its original path. Single file, exactly what iCloud handles well.
• A symlink in the project folder points to the database. The app sees `database.sqlite` where it expects, and underneath, that path resolves to the iCloud-synced file.

Also cleaned up the repo while I was there: the database, JSON/SQL backups, exported spreadsheets, even a screenshot — all tracked in the first commit. Removed them from tracking going forward, kept them on disk via `.gitignore`.

## Key Learnings
• iCloud silently evicts files it thinks aren't being used. For tens of thousands of tiny dependency files, this happens constantly and you never notice until something breaks
• Git tracking a database means every save is a commit and `git pull` clobbers local data — worst of both worlds
• SQLite is a single file, which is the sweet spot iCloud handles well
• Symlinks let you mix sync mechanisms without the app needing to know
• When two tools are doing the same job, the fix isn't to pick one — it's to draw a line between what each is good for

## Challenges
• The project was running inside a worktree of itself, and worktree git linkages use absolute paths — they break the moment you move the parent folder. Had to remove the worktree before any `mv`
• A normal fast-forward merge would have deleted the on-disk data files since the cleanup commit untracked them. Used a mixed reset + targeted checkout instead so the working tree stayed intact
• GitHub auto-created an "Initial commit" on the new repo, leaving local and remote histories divergent. Force-pushed since the remote stub had a 1-line auto-generated README and nothing of value

## Tech Decisions
• iCloud-synced SQLite over hosted DB: 5 minutes of setup vs. an hour of migration. Local-first is faster and works offline. The hosted option (Turso, Neon, Supabase) is the obvious upgrade when this app needs to run from a phone or a server
• Symlink over `DATABASE_PATH` env var: both work. Symlink keeps `.env` identical across devices, which is one fewer thing to remember
• Force-push over rebase: the remote stub had nothing worth preserving

## The Catch

Can't have the dev server running on both Macs at once. If two processes write through iCloud at the same time, the database file can corrupt. For a single-user app this is a discipline problem, not a real engineering problem — but it's the trade-off of choosing convenience over a hosted DB.

## Outcome

Started the morning broken, ended with clean separation. Code where it belongs, data where it belongs, the two no longer overlapping. The migration path to a hosted database is laid out clearly for the day it matters, but today is not that day.

---

May 5, 2026

Picked it up on the second Mac. Wanted to add this month's portfolio numbers. Clicked Save, saw the green ✅, refreshed... new month was gone.

The backend was lying. The bulk save endpoint was throwing on every request: someone had written it against Postgres (`db.execute`, `NOW()`) but the app's been on SQLite for a while. Every save was returning HTTP 400. But the frontend was unwrapping `res.json()` without checking `res.ok`, so the alert always showed success. Two bugs camouflaging each other. The endpoint was also silently dropping seven fields the form was sending. Three things wrong, all hidden by the UI happily lying.

A few hours in, `git status` showed every single file deleted. Index was empty. iCloud had stomped on `.git/index` mid-session. `git reset` rebuilt it from HEAD, working tree intact. No real damage, just a perfect demonstration of the iCloud-and-git problem I'd already known about in theory.

So I finished the migration the other Mac had already done: cloned the repo into `~/Projects` outside iCloud, symlinked `database.sqlite` back to its iCloud location, then nuked everything in the iCloud folder except the DB. Code through GitHub, data through iCloud, one symlink in between.

Takeaways:
• A "successful" UI doesn't mean a successful HTTP response. Always check `res.ok`.
• iCloud + git index is even more reliably broken than I thought. Not a sometimes thing.
• Two-device dev: the first 30 minutes on the second machine always pay off the "I'll set it up properly later" assumption.

Tomorrow: get the save-bug PR merged so both Macs can move off the feature branch.

projects.title: Planner and goal-tracker
projects.description:
February 20, 2026

I built a personal goals tracking system that manages my career progression from daily activities up to my 15-year vision. The system lets me log daily work, set weekly goals, track quarterly objectives, and maintain long-term visions for 2030, 2035, and 2040. Every Friday when I log my activities, it automatically generates a weekly overview markdown file and saves it to my Obsidian vault in the "Weekly B2B notes" folder.

I also integrated Claude AI so I can chat about my goals and progress. I can ask questions like "When did I last work on coffee-rater?" or "What activities aren't aligned with my long-term vision?" and Claude analyzes my last 30 days of activities and all my goals to give me contextual answers. The chat remembers our conversation and helps me stay aligned with my 2030/2035/2040 vision milestones.

---

March 5, 2026

AI chat button wasn't working. I had to update some packages to make it work again.

The fact that this chat works with my memories/notes from the past weeks and aligns them with future goals and can guide me on what is useful and what is not, is insane.

---

March 9, 2026

It looks like the automatic weekly summaries aren't being made, so I have to look into this. And while i'm doing this, I should probably include a check to complete missing info and see if I've crossed off all my weekly goals.

The easiest way for this, i think, is a screen with all the daily entries of the past 4 weeks. This way, I can edit and add information easily. I can also manually generate a summary for the missing weeks, once the info is completed.

---

March 15, 2026

"Really happy but looks like weekly and quarterly goals can't be checked off yet. Would need this capability + an overview of weekly goals that have or have not been accomplished + maybe some graphs.

Now I can chat with the AI to talk about my progress, but would be nice if i got feedback autonomously. One way is to have the AI link my weekly notes to my quarterly goals and long-term vision and write a few lines about that in the summary.

But I think i should also export a more comprehensive quarterly report based on everything from the past month. Should look into reports/frameworks to make the most of this."

Sent all of this to Claude in plan mode. GREAT decision as it mapped out changes and allowed me to fine-tune the next steps.

 Check-off weekly/quarterly goals — Checkbox forms on the dashboard toggle active ↔ completed. Failed goals show a red strikethrough with a "Mark done" button.                                                
  Weekly goals overview with chart — /history/weekly now shows a stacked Chart.js bar chart (completed/failed/active per week) and per-week completion badges ("2 / 3 done · 1 failed") with toggle buttons.       

  AI reflection in weekly Obsidian export — generateweeklyoverview() now calls Claude with your visions, quarterly goals, and week's activities to write a 2-3 sentence "Reflection" subsection at the top of the summary.

  Failed status for expired goals — expireoldgoals() runs on every dashboard load, auto-failing any weekly goal where week_end < today and any quarterly goal where the quarter has ended. Shown in red strikethrough everywhere.                                                                                                                                                                                           
    Quarterly report — "📊 Generate Quarterly Report" button in the footer. POSTs to /report/quarterly/export, calls Claude for Vision Alignment + Retrospective + Focus sections, interleaves OKR-style goal completion stats and week-by-week progress table, writes 2026 - Q1 quarterly review.md to your Obsidian weekly notes folder.

---

March 16, 2026

Also might need to look into the size of the database. at what stage does it become an issue? Perhaps I can clean the database's daily entries after 6 months since everything should be in Obsidian by then anyway. On the other hand, if it's just text entries, it doesn't take a lot of memory.

Feels like the summary is a python script, and not an AI summary because it's pretty long and almost identical to the daily entries...

---

March 24, 2026

Trying to hook up my calendar to create daily entries automatically. Accessing calendar didn't work so I gave up on this idea. It wouldn't have been such a timesaver anyway.

---

March 25, 2026

Added STT for larger text fields. This will make it much easier to input text and create more detailed daily entries. I'm also adding a short reflection form when creating a weekly review.

---

May 14, 2026

Quick session to close a gap from the last STT pass. The record button only showed up on a subset of fields, which kept catching me out. Anytime I wanted to dictate a goal title or use the weekly review screen, no button. Annoying enough that I finally fixed it.

Turned out the script was only attaching to textareas inside a specific form wrapper, and three templates didn't even load it. So I broadened the selector to cover every textarea and text input on the page, added an opt-out attribute in case I want to skip a field later, and pulled the script into the chat page, the weekly goals page, and the weekly review page.
• Most of the work was in the JS, not the templates. Templates only needed one extra script tag each.
• Added a check for flex parents so wrapping the field doesn't break inline layouts like the chat input row. That bit took the most thinking.
• Used a `data-no-stt` opt-out instead of trying to be clever about which fields "deserve" a button. Easier to add an attribute later than to chase a hidden allowlist.
• The chat input now has a record button too, which I didn't originally plan but realised I'd want.

Next time I touch this: the record button is a bit visually heavy below short title fields. Could shrink it or make it an icon when the field is a single-line input.

projects.title: Company finance tracking
projects.description:
February 9, 2026

I just realised that I don't have a solid view of my business expenses. I know that I typically earn more than I spend, but how much?
No better way to find out, than to vibe code a desktop app to keep track of invoices sent and received. 
Initially, it doesn't need to be complicated. The only tricky part is the difference between one-off expenses, and monthly, quarterly and yearly recurring ones. 

When this part works, I also want to develop a personal tracker. I've been tracking my investments in a Number sheet for over 10 years and it's getting kind of clunky. I'm also pretty sure there are some mistakes in my logic. So I can fix it and add it to my tracker.

Later on, if everything works, I could look at automating parts. I'm especially thinking about syncing expenses. Open banking is something I'm not going to get involved with, though.

This session, Claude generated:
• 26 Swift files (~3,700 lines of code)
• 24 source files
• 2 test files (30+ unit tests)
• 6 documentation files (comprehensive guides)
• 100% of planned features implemented

This version included an App with CloudKit. It sounded like an overkill for an app that just needs to sync between my devices, but what do I know? Only after trying to set it up in Xcode, my suspicions were confirmed.

It cost less than $5 so far. But it will probably end up costing a lot more as I need quite some back and forth to roll back Cloud capabilities that aren't available to free plans. Easily spent an extra hour on this as well. 

Damn, it looks like a real Apple App. Not what I expected but pretty nice apart from some alignment issues.

---

February 10, 2026

After some further back and forth, I got the app to work with decent padding too.

Now, I'm most definitely not going to use the same app for personal finances because it's going to break again. But I can use the structure and learnings from this to create another one.

Only thing left to do now is figure out how i can add this app to my desktop and how to give it a logo so I don't have to run it from Xcode every time.

---

Time to implement the next changes:
• net profit = difference between income and expenses without VAT
• (later include more detailed calculations for VAT based on category)
• Save names of expenses (eg charging) + detailed overview of expenses per name instead of category
• quarterly and yearly costs -> split over months but only if the expense is more than 250 euros.

 It worked pretty well but I had to delete the database and start from scratch since there was no database backup. Ah well, I didn't have that much in there yet anyway.

---

March 30, 2026

Last time, I had to delete the database and start from scratch, so please make a backup first today. And then I want to implement the following changes. 
• I want to see the income based on the issue date instead of the date, 
• the modal for inputting expenses has an issue when the number gets larger than 250 because then the accrued text shows and that causes the window to be too narrow. So the text then gets wider and the window is not wide enough. 
• I also want the possibility to add new categories myself and I want these to be reflected every where in the app.
• The fourth thing I want to add is that I want previous entries for company name and description to be viewable when I enter a new one, so maybe as a dropdown list or as some sort of cache that's filling while I'm typing.
• The next thing that I want to make available is 0% VAT on invoices because when I'm invoicing a foreign customer, I do not have to include VAT. 
• And finally, the number for the next invoice is not correct anymore because it only counts the number of existing invoices. It should just be plus one because i deleted the first invoice.

Also added an app icon. And removed wages from the graph of expenses because it was (i'm to ired to find the word) the graph.

---

May 2, 2026

Made the app look properly polished
• Cleaned up alignment everywhere — form fields now line up the way they should (the old version had a styling bug fighting against macOS's built-in form layout).
• Added a proper sidebar: app icon up top, color-coded section icons, a footer with version info, a wider default window.
• Tidied up every list — bigger search bar, cleaner toolbars with a divider, more breathing room between rows, monospaced numbers so amounts line up.
• Reworked the P/L Report into proper cards with consistent padding, icon tiles for the summary numbers, and tidy breakdown lists.

Added receipt and invoice scanning
• You can now scan a PDF or photo of a receipt (for expenses) or an invoice and the app auto-fills the form for you.
• It pulls amount, VAT rate, vendor/client, date, description, and invoice number when it can find them.
• Runs entirely on your Mac — no internet, no API keys, no cost.
• Lives as a subtle one-line bar at the top of the form: "Auto-fill from a PDF or image — Scan Receipt…". Click it, pick a file, fields fill in, you review and save.
• Only fills empty fields, so it never overwrites anything you've already typed.

Easy invoice status changes
• The status badge on each invoice row is now clickable — tap it and a menu pops up letting you switch between Draft, Sent, Paid, Overdue, Cancelled.
• Right-clicking a row also gives you the same menu plus a delete option.
• Switching to Paid auto-fills today's date; switching away clears it.

One small detour
• The first version of the scan bar I built was too loud — a big tinted banner that shouted at you every time you opened the form. You called it out, I made it a quiet single-line strip that fits the rest of the app.
learnings: I want to see the income based on the issue date instead of the date,

the modal for inputting expenses has an issue when the number gets larger than 250 because then the accrued text shows and that causes the window to be too narrow. So the text then gets wider and the window is not wide enough.

• Who had the most impressions last year? 

How does it work? 

Two simple n8n workflows. 
Every time a new success story gets added (or updated) to Webflow, it gets synced to a database 
Slack messages get passed on to an AI Agent who only takes the database as a single source of truth. The reply gets sent back to the same slack channel.

Pretty happy with the result.

April 2, 2026

Creating this assistant was pretty straightforward. I first made sure that all the older apps that I previously created and that it connects to run on different servers so they can all run at the same time. That was quick. 

Then I explained the idea of the marketing assistant that needs to access these three tools but also needs to be able to read from my Obsidian Vault and only my Obsidian Vault for certain questions. But then when it was finished, Laurens Nys shared a very timely post about the structuring of your information and notes etc. for AI agents.
